item.title: South American U20 Championship: CONMEBOL draw puts Brazil in Group B
item.description: South American U20 Championship: CONMEBOL draw puts Brazil in Group B Brazil will be the top seed in Group B of the 2027 South American Championship. The groups were decided in a draw held this Friday (13) at CONMEBOL headquarters in Asunción, Paraguay. Colombia is the top seed in Group A. The tournament will take place from January 22 to February 7 in Medellín. The top four teams in the competition’s final stage will qualify for the World Cup in this age group, which will take place in September in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan. Group B will feature Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia and Venezuela. Group A consists of Paraguay, Chile, Ecuador and Peru, alongside hosts Colombia. During the Brazilian Under-20 national team’s preparations in 2026, which included five squad call-ups, Brazil faced Bolivia twice at Granja Comary, winning both matches 2–0. Competition format The 2027 South American Under-20 Championship will be played in two stages: the group stage and the final stage. In the group stage, the ten participating teams are divided into Groups A and B, with five teams each. Matches will follow a single round-robin format, with every team playing each of the other teams in its group once. The top four teams in each group will advance to the final stage. In the final stage, the winner of each group will face the runner-up from the opposite group. The winners of these matches will automatically qualify for the World Cup and contest the tournament final. The losing semifinalists will face the winners of the crossover matches between the third- and fourth-placed teams in Groups A and B to determine the other two World Cup qualifiers. Unlike the Breeders' Cup, where entry primarily is through success in graded stakes races, the Claiming Crown heats are open only to horses who have started in claiming races for specific amounts in the recent past. Nine races, two of them on dirt, offer purses ranging up to $200,000 for the Claiming Crown Jewel on dirt and $175,000 for the Claiming Crown Emerald on turf. item.title: Former Michigan QB Colin Hurley plans to enter transfer portal
item.description: Former Michigan quarterback Colin Hurley plans to enter the transfer portal, his agent Brian Davis tells On3. Hurley previously medically retired due to a concussion but is ready to make his return to football. Hurley is a former four-star recruit and LSU transfer. Hurley has been enrolled at Michigan this fall, taking classes after medically retiring in the spring. Hurley transferred in from LSU this past offseason and went through winter conditioning and spring practices. The 6-foot-1, 218-pound Miami native spent two seasons with LSU, after reclassifying and joining the Tigers’ program at 16 years old in January 2024. “Colin has worked hard on his health and is excited to come back to the sport he loves,” Davis told On3. “Colin has two years of eligibility left and can’t wait to play again.” During the recruiting process, Hurley had interest from Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Miami, Ohio State and others. The former Jacksonville (Fla.) Trinity Christian Academy star was a two-time state champion in high shcool and threw for over 5,000 yards in his career. Hurley was also an Elite 11 finalist and a U.S. Army All-American. The college football transfer portal officially opens on Jan. 4 for a 10-day window.

item.title: Patriots takeaways from Germany: What Mike Vrabel said about A.J. Brown playing in Munich
item.description: MUNICH – After making the trip to Munich, will A.J. Brown play on Sunday against the Detroit Lions? That was the big question facing the Patriots on Friday. Temperatures dipped into the low 40s as the team held a full 90-minute practice at the FC Bayern Munich training facility. After flying into Munich on Thursday, and holding a 60-minute walkthrough, Mike Vrabel’s team picked up the pace. The Patriots coach said he felt “pretty good” about the status of A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson after watching the two players at Thursday’s practice. “So, let’s go through today and see where that goes and then meet with (trainer) Jim (Whalen) and meet with players,” Vrabel said. Brown has played in three of nine games this season. The Pro Bowl receiver missed four weeks in a row after suffering a high ankle sprain in the team’s regular-season opener in Seattle. After returning, and playing twice in five days, Brown’s been dealing with a nagging knee injury. The receiver missed two weeks of practices and the Patriots matchups against Miami and Green Bay. Brown returned to practice on Wednesday before flying with the team on Thursday. “I think the more that we can get everybody back, I think the more that it contributes to what we feel like we want to be as a team,” Vrabel said when asked about having Brown at practice. “And one guy certainly doesn’t make the difference, but it’s certainly the more that we can get guys back. It’s exciting that the pieces can start to build and come together. So, you know, we’ll see where things go today. And hopefully, you know, those guys that haven’t been with us or maybe got hurt last week, that could be available.” In three games, Brown’s caught nine passes for 101 yards. He’d be a huge boost for Drake Maye and the offense, if healthy. After dealing with two different injuries, Vrabel was asked if the team needed to protect Brown from himself when it comes to how much they play him when he does return. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino Leaves USMNT to Join Manchester United 1 Day After Club Fires Manager
item.description: Mega Mauricio Pochettino is saying goodbye to the United States men’s national team after just two years. U.S. Soccer announced during a press conference on Friday, November 13, that Pochettino, 54, would be stepping down to join Manchester United as its new manager. Pochettino called it “one of the most difficult decisions” to make, but added, “A decision that in some part is a sad decision, and in another part is we are professional and we are trying to find the next step and trying to make your dreams come true.” The news comes just one day after the Premier League team fired its former manager , Michael Carrick . Carrick was let go on November 12, just 15 games into his two-year contract, which he signed back in May. According to ESPN , a representative for Pochettino informed Manchester United of a $10 million release clause in his contract with U.S. Soccer, which United CEO Omar Berrada agreed to. Pochettino, who is from Argentina, was reportedly the only candidate to fill the vacant role and was the “unanimous choice” by the club’s leadership. Mega “The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players,” a statement from United read. “Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues.” Pochettino signed a 2.5 year deal with Man U and is set to take on his new role beginning when the team faces Liverpool in Anfield on November 22. item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Ayo Dosunmu has become a key player for the Minnesota Timberwolves this season. Anthony Edwards’ absence was viewed by many as a massive blow, and the Wolves did show some signs of weakness without their main man in attack. However, Dosunmu has taken much of that burden lately, and his performances for Chris Finch’s side have been really impressive. Now, the T-Wolves head coach has shared what separates him from many others. Chris Finch says Ayo Dosunmu’s ‘readiness factor is elite’ The Minnesota Timberwolves acquired Dosunmu from the Chicago Bulls in February this year. The former Illinois Fighting Illini star was initially brought in as a rotation option, but injuries to key players have often given him starting opportunities. Dosunmu has always been able to do a decent job for the Wolves, but his performances have gone up a level this season. Why? Finch believes it’s all down to his readiness factor – most players need some time to get going, but Dosunmu is different. He can hit the ground running at any point. Finch said in a press conference: “He has met every need that we’ve had along the way, whether it’d be a guy to come in and give us depth or step up in the playoffs when people went down, and now, without Anthony starting, just being the guy you can put the ball in his hands on demand and he gets you something. “He continues to have an end-to-end game and is a good fit alongside Melo in that regard. He fits so well with so many different lineups. You don’t even have to think about putting him out there to play on or off the ball. He’s just kind of met every moment we’ve needed him to meet. “He’s an unbelievable professional, and his readiness factor is elite. “A lot of players might spin their wheels a little bit before they’re able to produce what you need them to produce. He’s always been, right away, whatever we needed.” In his last eight games for the Timberwolves, Dosunmu has averaged 21.1 points, five rebounds and 3.2 assists. He has formed a great partnership with LaMelo Ball and is proving to be really effective. The Wolves have now won five games in a row. That is an impressive run on its own, but to do it without Edwards makes it so much better. Dosunmu deserves all the praise in the world, and if he can keep it going along with Ball, the T-Wolves will be in a great position by the time Edwards is back. item.description: Mauricio Pochettino struggled to fight off tears as he held his first press conference since being confirmed as Michael Carrick ’s managerial successor at Manchester United . Pochettino will leave his post as United States manager at the end of the current international break, joining up with United on 18 November after the club moved to replace Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday. Pochettino penned a four-year extension in the summer that was meant to keep him with the USA until the 2030 World Cup, but United triggered his release clause after a hashing out an agreement with the Argentinian, and will pay US Soccer compensation worth an initial $7m (£5.3m). Asked what made him swap the USA for United despite committing his future earlier this year, Pochettino said: "It's obvious. I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United. When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down. Mauricio Pochettino was in tears as he spoke for the first time since making the switch to Man United (Getty) "When we decided together to extend our commitment, it was a commitment for the federation, just in case. We were very committed. It was to help the federation, just in case that didn't work for four years." Pochettino said contact from United was first made on Sunday afternoon, the same day as the Villa draw, insisting that he was “very transparent” with US Soccer throughout the process. "All was so quick. Sunday afternoon, there started to be some contact. We were very transparent [with US Soccer],” he said. "We’ll have time next week to talk about the job at Manchester United. It’s much better to talk now about US Soccer." The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager nevertheless opted against speaking at length about his United move, which he described as “the most difficult decisions of my career”, instead focussing on Haiti and his time in the USA setup. "We have time this week to talk about the job in Manchester United but I think it's much better to talk about us, about US Soccer,” he said. “We have two games ahead and now it's focus on this." He will remain in charge for the United States’ two Concacaf Nations League fixtures against Haiti during the international break, with an away match on 14 November and a home match in Cincinnati on 18 November. Pochettino will then report to Carrington shortly after, with his official start date being on 18 November, ahead their next Premier League match against Liverpool at Anfield on 22 November. He also explained why he decided to see out the rest of the international break in the USA dugout, saying it was out of respect for his players and staff. item.title: Tearful Pochettino on 'difficult' decision to leave USA for Man Utd
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino was emotional during his USA news conference [Getty Images] Mauricio Pochettino says the decision to leave his role as boss of the USA national team to become Manchester United head coach was "one of the most difficult" of his career. The Argentine was announced as Michael Carrick's successor at Old Trafford on Friday, with sources telling BBC Sport he has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract. United paid a release clause in the region of £7.4m to extract Pochettino from his USA contract, with a further payment being made for his backroom staff. Pochettino only signed a new four-year deal with the USA in the summer, but will depart for Manchester after leading the national team in matches against Haiti on 14 and 18 November. The 54-year-old broke down in tears during his first news conference after his move to United was confirmed, and thanked the US Soccer Federation for its support. "It's difficult to talk now," he said. "I'm a very emotional guy. It's a very sad decision. "But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true." Asked why he signed a new deal with the national side only to accept United's offer, Pochettino said the chance to manage at Old Trafford was too good to reject. "I never said I wanted to go back but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United," he said. "When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down." Carrick was sacked on Thursday after United's worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years, which has left them languishing in 18th place in the Premier League. Pochettino will inherit a side that have won just once in 10 league matches this season and sit just one point above bottom-placed Sunderland. His first match in charge will be an away match against Liverpool on 22 November. How Ferguson-inspired Pochettino can succeed where Carrick failed at Man Utd A decade in the making Pochettino's arrival at Old Trafford marks the end of a decade-long courtship. Thriving during an 18-month stint at Southampton, he led the Saints to eighth place during his only full season on the south coast. Tottenham moved quickly to appoint one of the most promising young coaches in Europe in 2014, and it was in north London that his reputation rocketed. The club had finished in the top four just twice in the 22 years before his appointment, but Pochettino led them there four times in his five full seasons. It was two years into his time in the capital that United first considered a move for Pochettino. The Argentine dined with legendary former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson in Mayfair, London just weeks before Louis van Gaal was sacked as Red Devils boss. The club ultimately decided to appoint Jose Mourinho, and Pochettino was again overlooked when the Portuguese departed in 2018, with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer impressing so much in an interim role that he was given the job more permanently. item.title: Dan Campbell pitches football, Lions to German fans
item.description: MUNICH, Germany — Between his time as a player, assistant and now a head coach, Dan Campbell is approaching three decades spent in the NFL. All that time in and around football makes Campbell uniquely qualified to pitch the game he loves to Germans, many of whom are being introduced to the sport for the first time this week, as the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots will play at Allianz Arena on Sunday, Nov. 15. "This game gave me a life," Campbell said Friday, Nov. 13, addressing reporters in Munich. "I was not a superstar, I was not a speed demon. I've got size, I played tight end, so you do a little bit of everything. But it gave me an opportunity to make a life and do something I absolutely loved with a group of guys, in any given time, 53 men in that locker room that you all have the same goal and you're all going in the same directions, and the blood and the sweat and the tears that it requires on a daily basis to be great are the things you never forget." Added Campbell, who tapped his fist on the table in front him as he became more fired up: "It builds character. It builds character in your team, it builds character as an individual, and it allows you to overcome anything in life that may come your way. Unfortunately, and I tell the team all the time, one day you're gonna get hit, you're gonna get rocked with something really tough in your life. I hate to say it, I don't want it to happen, none of us do, but you will, and you're going to have to be the rock. "But you're going to know how to overcome it, and you know who you can lean on, too, your brothers who have gone through everything you had to go through here. I just think it's special that way, and it gives guys an opportunity that may not have all the bells and whistles, all that, just because they do all the little things right and they maximize everything that they have and their ability. That's the best way I could do it or say it." item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards.
